// Debugger: These use CodeLLDB (vadimcn.vscode-lldb). The `cargo` key needs rust-analyzer's companion support; if your setup lacks it, run the matching task first and point `program` at target/debug/<binary>.
// Where the installs are: From .env at the top of the repository, the same file docker-compose.yml reads. `envFile` puts both paths in the debugged process's environment; `${env:...}` in `args` is resolved by VS Code from its OWN environment, which inside the devcontainer is what docker-compose.yml's `environment:` block sets. On a bare host, export them before starting VS Code: `set -a; . ./.env; set +a; code .` -- otherwise --game arrives empty and daysengine says it found no install.
// Why both titles: Shiny Days is a second title on the same engine, not a variant. Every screen is its own recovery, so a change is not verified until it has been seen on the one it was recovered from.

configurations.name: Play: School Days HQ
configurations.// Opens a window: One binary does both: with no subcommand it plays, and takes over the desktop. Prefer an inspection configuration below unless you are debugging the window, the GPU path or input.

configurations.name: daysengine (inspection subcommands)
configurations.// The verification path: Headless: composites a screen, parses a script, reads the save, and prints what it found. Everything here can be checked from a test or a diff.

inputs.// Either title: Prefilled with DAYS_GAME_DIR; paste DAYS_SHINYDAYS_DIR's value to inspect the other install. Both are in .env, and both are the same path inside the devcontainer as outside it.
inputs.description: Game directory (the one holding Packs and the game executable)

inputs.// How a screen is reached: `menu` starts at the title and is driven by events, because that is how a player reaches a screen. There is no mode argument: the state machine decides, which is the thing being verified.
inputs.description: Menu events, comma separated (down, up, enter, esc, click:X:Y, ...). Empty for the title as it opens.
